issues.description: The problem statement requires a Bookstore that holds an array of Books named `books` and an initializer `init(books: [Book])`. The provided solution's Bookstore implementation declares the stored property as `inventory: [Book]` but the initializer assigns to `self.books = books`, and the solution's Client accesses `bookstore.books`. This name mismatch (property `inventory` vs expected `books`) is a structural inconsistency that will cause compilation errors and confuse students about the correct property name to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure a consistent property name across specification, template, and solution. Update the Bookstore implementation to declare `let books: [Book]` and make the initializer assign to `self.books = books`, or alternatively update the problem statement and client to expect `inventory` everywhere. Prefer changing the Bookstore implementation to use `books` to match the problem description and client usage.

issues.description: The problem statement requires the Bookstore to hold an array named `books` and an initializer `init(books:)`. In the solution implementation the Bookstore class declares the property under a different name (`inventory`) while other parts of the solution (the initializer and Client) still refer to `books`. This inconsistent naming of the same conceptual property (the bookstore's collection of Book objects) across artifacts creates confusion for students mapping the requirement (`books`) to the implementation (`inventory`) and introduces an internal mismatch in the solution itself.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single, consistent name for the Bookstore's collection across all artifacts. Rename the solution's `inventory` property to `books` (i.e., `let books: [Book]`) and ensure the initializer and all references use `books`, matching the problem statement and tests. Alternatively, if `inventory` is preferred, update the problem statement and all client/test code to refer to `inventory` — but keeping `books` is recommended to match the stated requirement.
